title: B's landmark notes chatter when the hand rests on ¼, ½ or ¾: about 38 notes a second from a 1 px tremor
detail: B rings a landmark whenever t crosses 0, ¼, ½, ¾ or 1 exactly (engine_b.js scrub(): T0 < m && T1 >= m, or the reverse). There is no hysteresis. The notes are forced, so the gap and the storm guard never apply. They are also marked count:true, so they never soften on repeats. People aim for ½ and stop there, and a resting hand or trackpad shakes by a pixel (0.0011 of t on a 900 px slider). Each shake re-rings the note. A has no such problem at a landmark, because its detent rounding (Math.round(20 t)) puts the boundary 0.025 away from the landmark. This brings back the chatter the user complained about, in the place where the hand rests. The board's 'wiggle' demo (±0.13) and MEASUREMENTS §1 do not show it.
evidence: c3.js: 60 slider inputs at 16 ms intervals (1.57 s), alternating t = 0.25 ± 0.0005. B: 60 landmark cues. A: 1 cue. At t = 0.5 ± 0.0011 (a 2 px tremor): B 60, A 1. A's own weak spot, a tremor across a non-landmark boundary (0.325 ± 0.0005), gives 60 calls and 16 played (its 40 ms gap). c2.js also posted about 120 landmark cues at 0 dB in about 1 s while two tremor loops overlapped. Scripts: scratchpad/rprod/c2.js and c3.js (the CDP daemon on port 9055).
fix: Re-arm a landmark only after t has left it by at least 0.02, as A's rounding does. Also allow at most one landmark per 120 ms unless it is a different landmark. Add a tremor case to the board's 'Drag for me' buttons ('rest on ½') and to measure.js, so that the comparison shows it.

title: B has no hush: Esc does nothing, off is slow, and queued cues survive both
detail: The app's rules (DESIGN §1.2, rules 4, 5 and 7) say that Esc stops any playback, queued bell or tone at once; that off cuts within about 10 ms and stops every scheduled source; and that a hidden tab hushes and suspends. SoundB exports no hush or stop. The worklet's cue list has no 'clear' message. SoundB.set({on:false}) only ramps the master gain with a 30 ms time constant (about 140 ms to −40 dB). Queued turn bells (up to 1 s) and loop pings stay in the worklet, so they play if sound comes back on soon after. Neither engine_b.js nor page.js listens for Escape, visibilitychange or pagehide. On the board, Esc does nothing in either palette, and there is no Sound off control, so the user cannot check 'Esc and off are silent' for B. v2 DESIGN §7 (Building it) does not mention any of this.
evidence: c2.js: B ×4 on 'Toggle on', Escape pressed 150 ms in: 3 of the 4 cues were posted after Esc. Code: engine_b.js has no hush, stop, Escape or visibility handler (grep). SoundB.set uses setTargetAtTime(…, 0.03). A (notes/v15-candidate/src/sound.js:312–320, 818) has hush(), a visibilitychange hush plus suspend, and a pagehide hush.
fix: Add a {k:'clear'} message that empties the worklet's cues and textures, starting the tails with a short raised-cosine fade. Call it from SoundB.hush(), and route that through the graph's existing bus hush. Clear the turn and contour queues. On the board, wire Esc to Sound.hush() + SoundB.hush() and also cancel the ×4 timers, the Play and the auto-drag. Add a Sound on/off switch to the bar. Add the hush and the hidden tab to the §7 build list and to the click regressions.

title: The first press in B is silent; the first press in A plays: a biased first impression
detail: start() runs in a capture listener on the first pointerdown or keydown and calls SoundB.ensure(), which loads the worklet asynchronously. The press's own handler runs before the engine exists, so SoundB.play returns false and nothing sounds. A plays its first press (the gesture exception in its own rules). With the keyboard (Enter on a button), the click fires in the same task as the keydown, so B's first press is always silent. A user who starts in B, which is the default palette, hears nothing on the first try. They may think B is broken or too quiet.
evidence: c2.js, fresh page: a click on the B button of 'Toggle on' left SoundB's log at 0 entries, still 0 after 600 ms; the second click logged 1. Enter on the same button with focus: 0 entries. c3.js, fresh page: the first click on A's button played (Sound.play returned true).
fix: In the board: if SoundB is not ready, keep the last request and play it when ensure() resolves, within 300 ms of the gesture. Or start both engines on page load with a visible 'Start sound' button that is the first thing to press. For the app, B's engine must keep A's rule that the 'on' confirmation is heard.

title: Pressing B again makes it quieter (up to −4 dB), so 'press it several times' breaks the loudness match
detail: B's 'repetition softens' rule (−1 dB per repeat within 2 s, down to −4 dB) also applies to auditions in the cue table. The table text asks the user to 'press it several times, or use ×4'. A never softens. So B's ×4 plays at 0, −1, −2 and −3 dB, and a fifth quick press at −4 dB, while A's plays stay level. Quieter often reads as 'nicer' or 'less tiring'. This undoes the cue-by-cue level matching that MEASUREMENTS §3 reports. It is a real feature of B, but on the board it reads as timbre when it is level.
evidence: c2.js: the gains B posted for ×4 on 'Toggle on' were −1.07, −2.07, −3.07 and −4.07 dB (TRIM −1.07, then 0, −1, −2, −3 for the repeats). engine_b.js play(): rg = −min(4, k) when !d.count && !o.noRep. page.js cueB does not pass noRep.
fix: Pass noRep:true for single auditions in the table. Give ×4 a small switch, 'with B's repeat softening', off by default, or say in the table: 'B gets up to 4 dB softer when repeated within 2 s; A does not.'

title: The glass choir's random level drift (1.6 to 3.5 dB) is as large as the meaningful loudness range of the tone (4.9 dB)
detail: In the app, the Shepard tone's loudness and brightness carry |F|: −36.7 LUFS near a zero, −32.9 at |F| = 1 and −31.8 near a pole, a 4.9 dB range (DESIGN §2.2). B adds a slow random level change: 1.6 dB at rest and 3.5 dB on a loop (MEASUREMENTS §4). It also adds a ±0.06 octave wander of the bell's centre, which is the parameter that moves with ln|F|. A listener who follows the tone getting quieter toward a zero, for example a screen-reader user with the keyboard probe, can no longer tell drift from approach. The pitch and winding stay exact, which is good, but 'animated' should not add noise to a channel that carries meaning.
evidence: MEASUREMENTS.md §4: 'slow level change' A 0.15 / 0.14 dB, B 1.6 / 3.5 dB. DESIGN.md §2.2 table, Shepard voice range 4.9 dB. engine_b.js lines 183–188 (detune ±1.5 cents, level ±0.06, colour ±0.06 octave).
fix: Keep the beating and the vibrato, and cap the slow level change at about 1 dB, under a fifth of the meaningful range. Cut the amplitude drift from ±0.06 to ±0.02 and the colour wander from ±0.06 to ±0.02 octave. Re-measure. Or turn the drift off while the keyboard probe is in use.

title: The A/B switch is hard to see in dark mode, and its keyboard focus ring is clipped
detail: This switch is the board's most important control. In dark mode the pressed segment is white text on --a #9fb0c2 (2.2:1) or on --b #7cc4b2 (2.0:1), under the 4.5:1 of WCAG 1.4.3. The pressed state, which says which palette you are hearing, is the hardest text on the page to read. Its focus ring (2 px, offset 2 px) is drawn outside the button, inside a .seg with overflow:hidden. Only a sliver at one edge shows (WCAG 2.4.7). The same clipping affects the other segmented groups (play length, B's slider mode, function, view).
evidence: Contrast computed from page.html's tokens: dark A pressed 2.22, dark B pressed 2.02 (light: 5.53 and 5.88). Screenshots shots/dark_bar.png, dark_focus.png and light_focus.png in scratchpad/rprod/rprod_cdp: after two Tabs, focus is on 'B · new' and only a thin line at its left edge is visible. Computed style: outline solid 2px with offset 2px; the parent has overflow hidden.
fix: In dark mode, use dark text on the light accents (#141412 on #9fb0c2 is about 9:1), or keep white text and darken the pressed fill. Use outline-offset:-3px for buttons inside .seg, or drop overflow:hidden and round the end buttons instead.

title: On a phone, the cue table's play buttons are all off-screen, and the sticky bar takes 126 px
detail: The table has min-width 560 px inside a horizontal scroller. At 375 px wide, the A, ×4, B and ×4 buttons start at x = 414. The user sees the cue names and a cut-off 'What it means' column, and no buttons, with no hint that the table scrolls sideways. The sticky bar wraps to three rows (126 px, 16 % of an 812 px screen) for the whole visit. On the first screen, the intro and the hint fill the space, and the slider the user complained about starts below the fold.
evidence: c1.js at 375 × 812 (mobile emulation): .tbl-wrap scrollWidth 560 against clientWidth 309; first row buttons at x 414, 452, 507 and 544; bar height 126; morph canvas at y 666. Screenshots shots/phone_top.png and shots/phone_cues.png.
fix: Below 600 px, show each cue as a row of name and buttons, with the meaning on a second line, and no table. Make the bar one row on a phone: the A/B switch and the volume only. Move the 'press A / B' hint and the status into the page. Put the slider card directly under a one-line intro.

title: 'Hear the function' cannot be tried with the keyboard or on a touch screen
detail: The plane canvas has tabindex=0 but no key handler. A keyboard or screen-reader user can focus it and nothing happens, though the app's keyboard probe (arrows, Z, O, Enter) is how they would actually use this tier. It also matters for the choir, whose vibrato needs about 0.7 s of rest, longer than the app's 280 ms keyboard samples. On a touch screen there is no hover: pointerdown immediately starts a loop. Every touch-drag therefore ends with a winding-number cue (often the W = 0 knock), and the instructions ('Hover', 'Rest the pointer') cannot be followed.
evidence: page.js: no keydown listener on #planeCv; pointerdown always sets P.loop (lines 184–187); pointerup plays loopDone when more than 8 points were drawn (line 193).
fix: Add arrow-key steps (0.1, Shift 0.02) that call hover() and sound a 280 ms sample as in the app, with Enter to start and close a loop and the readout in a polite live region. On touch, a press without movement for 300 ms should start a loop; a drag right away should probe. Or add a 'Draw a loop' switch. Say in one line which gesture does what on touch.

title: The cue table's buttons are named only 'A', '×4', 'B' and '×4' for screen readers
detail: Each of 24 rows has four buttons with the same four names, so a screen reader's button list is 96 entries of A, times 4, B and times 4 with no cue. The palette switch's status (#status) is not a live region, so switching with the A or B key is not announced. The A and B keys are also screen-reader browse-mode quick keys: B is 'next button' in NVDA and JAWS, so there they do not switch the palette. Single-character shortcuts with no way to turn them off fail WCAG 2.1.4.
evidence: page.js line 237 (the row template); page.html #status has no aria-live or role; page.js line 30 (window keydown for a/b, with no modifier and no focus condition).
fix: Use aria-label='Play “Toggle on” in A' and 'Play “Toggle on” in A, four times', or put the cue name in a th scope='row' and give the buttons aria-describedby. Make #status role='status'. Keep A/B, but only when focus is not in a form control, and add Alt+A/Alt+B or a note that the switch buttons are the way.

title: Switching palettes during a play mixes them; 'Loop' gives silence to compare after the first pass
detail: Switching A/B while something plays is the natural way to compare, but here it gives a hybrid. Press Play in B, press A at 0.7 s: B's motion bed keeps running for the rest of the pass (the step loop checks p.pal, not PAL), then A's arrival plays. Pause after switching skips SoundB.motionEnd() (it checks PAL), though the texture's 250 ms hold silences it anyway. With Loop on, repeats are silent in both palettes (the app's rule), so a looping comparison is silent after the first pass in either palette.
evidence: c2.js: Play in B, key 'a' at 700 ms: 79 B motion-bed messages after the switch, and A's Sound.play('morphEnd') at the arrival. page.js lines 84, 96 and 99.
fix: On a palette switch, stop Play and any auto-drag (stopPlay(); stopAuto()) and say 'Switched to A: press Play'. Or restart the same play in the new palette from t = 0. Remove Loop from the board, or label it 'Loop (silent after the first pass, as in the app)'.

title: 'Notes only' still plays the air during Play
detail: B's slider mode 'notes only' (C) is for someone who wants near-silence (v2 DESIGN §3). SoundB.motion() ignores the mode, so pressing Play in C still plays the motion bed. Anyone who picks C in order to compare 'notes only' hears the air when they press Play.
evidence: c2.js: mode C, Play 2 s: 121 motion-bed messages, v = 0.5. engine_b.js line 488 has no mode check, while scrub() checks mode === 'B'.
fix: Skip the motion bed when mode is C, or rename the option to 'slider: notes only' and say that the play sound is the same.

title: The page leans toward B; a blind option would make the user's choice more trustworthy
detail: B is the default palette. It is labelled 'new', its slider mode is labelled '(recommended)', and A's slider is described in the section that 'cracks'. Expectation bias in listening tests is large; this is why BS.1116 and MUSHRA use hidden references. The user asked for sounds that feel nicer, and nobody here has heard B, so their ear is the whole verdict.
evidence: page.html: data-p='B' aria-pressed='true' by default; '(recommended)'; h2 '1. The Deformation (the slider that "cracks")'.
fix: Add a 'Blind' switch: the top switch shows X / Y, assigned at random on each page load, with a 'Reveal' button and a one-tap 'I prefer X / Y' choice. Start in A, the familiar sound. Move '(recommended)' to the reveal.

title: Order and text: the opening hint is overwritten, and 'Hear the function' (off by default) comes before the interface (heard most)
detail: The first instruction, 'Try the slider below in A, then in B…', is replaced at load by 'Palette B: the new sounds…', because init calls setPal('A'); setPal('B'). The user chose Interface and Events on, and Hear the function off. So the sounds they live with are sections 1 and 3, yet section 2 is the off-by-default tier, with the longest instructions (about 66 words). The board's 'Hear the function' switch is on, which does not match the app and is not explained. The intro is 65 words and includes 'timbre' and 'struck and bowed materials'.
evidence: c1.js: the hint text at load is 'Palette B: the new sounds. Each play is a little different.' Section order: 1 Deformation, 2 Hear the function, 3 Interface, 4 Every cue. Paragraph word counts: 65, 49, 66, 20, 37, 17.
fix: Initialise with no setPal calls, or set the hint after them. Order: 1 the slider, 2 the interface, 3 every cue, 4 'Hear the function (off by default in the app)'. Cut the intro to two lines: 'Switch A (today) / B (new) at the top. Try the slider first.'

title: The slider's air sound is in Mathematical events, so it cannot be turned off without losing the loop pings
detail: The air texture is gesture feedback for the hand, not a mathematical event, yet it rides the events tier, along with the landmarks and the loop-closed winding pings. Someone who finds the air tiring has only one switch, and it also takes away the winding number of a loop. This affects how B would sit in the app's tier switches.
evidence: engine_b.js scrub(): tex tier 1 (events), gated by tierOn('events'); CAT.loopDone tier 'events'.
fix: Put the air under Interface (it is the hand's feedback). Or make 'Slider sound: air + notes / notes only / off' a setting in the Sound popover, as the board already does.

title: Small accessibility and phone details: switch contrast, small targets, the dimmed row, the choir's pan, iPhone silence
detail: (a) The track of an off switch is --line on the card: 1.33:1 (1.24:1 on the page background). WCAG 1.4.11 asks for 3:1. (b) The chips' × buttons are 20 × 15 px (WCAG 2.5.8 asks for 24 × 24). (c) In A, 'B's slider' row is dimmed to 45 % opacity, which the app's own DESIGN §2.1 rejects ('no opacity dimming: dimmed text measured 2.4:1'). (d) The choir spreads its side voices ±0.25 around the voice's pan and clamps at ±0.6, while A caps voices at ±0.3 so that one earbud keeps everything. The side voices are about 15 dB under the main one, so the loss is small, but the rule changes. (e) On an iPhone with the silent switch on, neither palette sounds, and the board does not say why (the app's popover has this note).
evidence: Contrast from page.html's tokens. c1.js at 375 px: the × buttons are 20 × 15. page.js line 25 (opacity 0.45). engine_b.js line 248: clamp(pan + SPR[m], −0.6, 0.6), against sound.js clamp(pn, −0.3, 0.3) at lines 567 and 577.
fix: (a) Give the off track a 3:1 border (--mut). (b) Make the × buttons 24 × 24. (c) Show 'applies to B' instead of dimming. (d) Clamp the side voices at ±0.3 + 0.1, or narrow the spread when |pan| > 0.2. (e) Add a one-line note under the bar on iOS: 'No sound? Turn off the silent switch.'
